messages:
laura wang: incident-bot just opened an incident for p99 timeouts on /v1/embeddings from the canary deploy. Paging @sre-oncall and @aj patel :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INCIDENT #2142 created — severity: P1 — symptom: elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts on embeddings (canary). Pager notified: sre-oncall.
sre-oncall: seeing it. p95 up ~2x, p99 up ~6x on canary nodes only. Canary weight 10%. Rolling back?
aj patel: need quick triage — is it model slower or gateway errors? I see a lot of 504 from gateway logs.
maria gonzalez: pulling logs from gateway-canary-01 now. There are repeated "upstream read timeout" lines and connection pool saturation traces.
james park: can confirm: connection_pool.active=256, pool.max=256, new connections failing with ECONNRESET. Looks like our gateway health-check concurrency + new canary connections saturating backend slots.
laura wang: customer impact: support-ops reporting multiple customer requests failing to embed on hosted-api region-us-west-2. Some customers seeing degraded throughput and retries.
support-ops: a handful of customers (acct IDs masked) reported 503s starting ~2142000008. One high-volume tenant saw 30% request loss for 3m. We're posting to status page draft.
aj patel: mitigation options: 1) immediate canary rollback 2) increase gateway connection pool on canary hosts 3) enable degrade-to-legacy-model fallback for embeddings route. Which do we do in parallel?
sre-oncall: start rollback now. aj — can you patch gateway pool while rollback proceeds so we have a safe next attempt?
aj patel: rolling back canary: deploying previous revision to canary hosts (cmd: \`releases promote --target=canary --from=stable --rev=20260314.8\`). Kicking now.
incident-bot: Deploy job queued: release 20260314.8 -> canary. CI checks pass.
maria gonzalez: starting gateway pool bump — patching configmap on canary group: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  gateway.maxConnections: "512"
  gateway.idleTimeoutMs: "60000"
```
Applying now.
laura wang: alerting customers via status: slight degraded performance for embeddings, mitigation in progress.
sre-oncall: rollback in progress — monitoring p99. If p99 drops under SLO threshold after rollback, we'll keep rollback and follow up.
(2m pass)
james park: rollback finished and stable nodes now serving canary traffic back to stable revision. p95 back to normal, p99 dropped from ~4.8s to ~180ms. 5xxs trending to baseline.
support-ops: customers reporting recovered. Updating status to "service partially recovered" and will follow up with postmortem later.
aj patel: gateway pool bump didn't apply fast enough to be useful for this window — good call to rollback first. We should still keep the pool change in a hotfix branch and run a controlled load test.
maria gonzalez: captured logs and heap of traces from canary instances. Looks like a connection storm on model-loader client when embeddings model warmed up — KV cache priming + sudden burst = backend thread pool exhaustion.
laura wang: ACTIONS: 1) run load-resilience test against gateway + model-loader priming by next sprint (owner: aj). 2) Add circuit-breaker to embeddings route to shed new model loads (owner: maria). 3) Update rollout checklist to include staggered model warmup (owner: laura). 4) Postmortem with timeline and customer impact (owner: laura).
aj patel: I'll open an RFC for connection pool defaults and a short-term hotfix to increase pool size on Dedicated gateways. Also schedule canary duration increase to capture these flakiness windows.
incident-bot: Severity changed: P1 -> P2 (service recovered). Incident will remain open until postmortem filed.
james park: saving log sample and grepping for "upstream read timeout" and "connection_pool" — attaching snippet to incident.
maria gonzalez: note: we saw spike right after model swap (00:08 after deploy), so sequence is deploy -> model swap -> KV cache fill -> connection storm. Recommend adding throttled priming for warmup.
sre-oncall: good post-incident notes. Handoff to oncall followup board. If anything flares up revert plan is in place.
laura wang: thanks everyone — great fast coordination. Will draft postmortem with timeline and customer table. :thumbsup:
support-ops: closing customer-facing thread, will send follow-up emails to impacted tenants with link to incident postmortem when ready.
incident-bot: Incident #2142 status: mitigated — awaiting postmortem.
